chapter: Ellington band: drinking, quarrels and rent parties
title: Cutting contests rather than jam sessions, and his debut at Mexico's
summary: Horn players did not play rent parties; cutting contests at Mexico's in the basement had a night for each instrument, and that was Bigard's New York debut before he went to the Nest.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did very many members of the band play rent parties? Was it mainly a piano player's function or --
-- did some of the horn players also play, too?

In those days it wasn't jam sessions. They used to call them "cutting contests." You see, the guys outplay each other with the same instrument. See, like here they have jam sessions where you'll have a band having a jam session. But there was a place called Mexico and each night would be a night for different instruments. One night was sax and one trumpet, trombone, piano, like that. Clarinet. So that's where I made my debut.
Uh-huh, in Mexico's. That's down in the basement, the gin mill.

Yeah. And then I went to work at a place called The Nest, an after-hour place, before I joined Duke.
